overall: The AG found no violation on the claim that the Chair read an unnoticed memo, since no real deliberation occurred. It separately found, on its own initiative, that the in-person meeting was not accessible to the public because of a capacity limit and no alternative access. It issued a reminder rather than an order.

allegations.summary: Chair read aloud a Town Administrator memo about a public records request at the August 20 meeting without listing the topic on the posted notice.
allegations.key_passage: Where a public body does not actually engage in any deliberation on a particular topic, it cannot violate the Open Meeting Law with respect to whether that particular topic should have been included on the meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Meeting was held in person with a 12-person capacity limit, members of the public were turned away or asked to leave, and no remote access was offered. Raised by the AG, not the complaint.
allegations.key_passage: In doing so, the Board denied members of the public access to its meeting.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
